voice.instructions: Warm, clear explainer narrator. Friendly and curious, measured pace.

scenes.label: Opening
scenes.narration: This is a Claude skill for making explainer videos. No video model is involved. Every frame you're watching is a web page.
scenes.visual: Condensed two-line headline. 'Every frame' (~4s): a pencil note and arrow point at the running timecode. 'web page': browser chrome with the render URL slides in above the headline.

scenes.label: Storyboard
scenes.narration: It starts with a storyboard. Claude plans each scene, with its narration and what should be on screen, then writes every scene as a small JavaScript module.
scenes.visual: Left: a video.json scene entry. Right: three sketched storyboard panels draw themselves. Narration and visual lines get highlighted as they're named. 'JavaScript module': a scene file name appears under each panel.

scenes.label: Timeline
scenes.narration: Scenes draw with HTML and SVG, and animate on GSAP timelines. The timelines stay paused, so any moment can be recreated exactly, just by seeking to it.
scenes.visual: Top: a demo square and dot. Bottom: a timeline track with three tween bars and a playhead. The playhead sweeps and drives the demo. 'stay paused': it stops. 'seeking to it': it jumps to three times and the demo snaps to match, each jump tagged seek(t).

scenes.label: Render
scenes.narration: To render, Playwright drives headless Chromium. It seeks one frame, takes a screenshot, and pipes it into ffmpeg. Four browsers work in parallel, so a minute of video renders in about a minute.
scenes.visual: Pipeline left to right: Chromium, a moving film strip of frames, ffmpeg, video.mp4. 'Four browsers': Chromium becomes four stacked workers and the strip speeds up. 'about a minute': the measured figure, 1,950 frames in 49 seconds.

scenes.label: Review
scenes.narration: Before the final render, Claude checks its own work. A linter flags layout and timing mistakes, and a contact sheet shows the whole video at a glance.
scenes.visual: Left: lint output with two warnings highlighted. Right: a contact sheet grid fills in; one tile is outlined as a fault, then fixed.

scenes.label: Voice
scenes.narration: The voiceover comes from OpenRouter, using models like ElevenLabs or Gemini. Pauses measured in the audio let each animation land on the word it shows, like this one.
scenes.visual: Model names appear. The real waveform of this narration draws, with a playhead following the voice. 'Pauses measured': the gaps are highlighted. 'like this one': a highlighter sweeps over those exact words.

scenes.label: Recap
scenes.narration: Write the storyboard, render the frames, add a voice. Ask Claude for an explainer, and this is what you get.
scenes.visual: Three steps in sequence, popping on each phrase. Then the closing line and the repo name.
